CAUSE: The likely root cause is the 15-second subprocess timeout in `app.merge_test_gate._git()` at `app/merge_test_gate.py:153-160`. `changed_paths()` calls it at line 189 to run `git diff --name-only <target-sha>...HEAD`. With 2,402 changed files, including many images and renames, Git can exceed that timeout. `_git()` then returns `None`, and `app.merge_operations._prepare_admission_snapshot()` converts that into “cannot derive target-relative merge paths” at `app/merge_operations.py:858-864`. Retries fail identically because the workload and timeout are unchanged.

The teammate’s merge-base guess is unsupported: `changed_paths()` does not explicitly compute a merge base. It uses Git’s three-dot diff syntax, which computes the merge base internally; there is no code here that turns an empty path list into this error. The error is raised only when `changed_paths()` returns `None`.

Recommended fix: derive paths with a scalable, NUL-delimited Git command and give that operation an appropriate timeout (or avoid imposing the generic 15-second timeout). Preserve rename handling and distinguish subprocess timeout/errors from an empty successful diff so the gate can report the actual failure.
